Let \(a,b,c\) be the amounts held by A, B, C.

\[
a+\frac12 b+\frac12 c=90 \implies 2a+b+c=180
\]
\[
b+\frac12 a+\frac12 c=70 \implies a+2b+c=140
\]
\[
c+\frac12 a+\frac12 b=56 \implies a+b+2c=112
\]

Subtract the second equation from the first:

\[
a-b=40 \implies a=b+40
\]

Subtract the third from the second:

\[
b-c=28 \implies c=b-28
\]

Substitute into \(2a+b+c=180\):

\[
2(b+40)+b+(b-28)=180
\]
\[
4b+52=180
\]
\[
4b=128
\]
\[
b=32
\]

\boxed{32}
